steps: 1. Write regression test TestBusUnsubscribeAfterCloseMustNotPanic in bus_test.go that calls bus.Unsubscribe(kind, handler) after bus.Close() and asserts no panic. This test MUST fail before the fix (nil map dereference in Unsubscribe line 113).

2. Write regression test TestBusFlushAfterCloseMustNotPanic in bus_test.go that calls bus.Flush() after bus.Close() and asserts no panic. This test MUST fail before the fix (nil map iteration in Flush line 146).
3. Fix Bus.Unsubscribe in bus.go: add `if b.subs == nil { b.mu.Unlock(); return }` guard immediately after acquiring b.mu.Lock on line 112, before accessing b.subs[kind] on line 113.
4. Fix Bus.Flush in bus.go: add `if b.subs == nil { b.mu.Unlock(); return }` guard immediately after acquiring b.mu.Lock on line 144, before the range loop over b.subs on line 146.
5. Request host gate: go test ./internal/events/... -race -count=1 to verify both new regression tests pass and all existing tests remain green.
6. Request host gate: go vet ./internal/events/... to verify no static analysis findings.
7. If host gates fail, inspect failure output, fix only the reported issue, and re-request the failing gate.
summary: Scope: confirmed nil-map panic bug in Bus.Unsubscribe and Bus.Flush when called after Bus.Close. Changed files: internal/events/bus.go (two nil guards added), internal/events/bus_test.go (two new regression tests). Bug: Bus.Close sets b.subs=nil after draining delivery goroutines, but Unsubscribe and Flush access b.subs without nil checks. Reachable via MetricsAdapter.Close() after bus.Close(), and directly by any caller calling Unsubscribe/Flush after Close. Existing test TestMetricsAdapter_CloseAfterBusClose documents this must not panic. Fix: two nil-guard returns after the mutex lock in both methods. Tests: (1) TestBusUnsubscribeAfterCloseMustNotPanic — subscribes handler, closes bus, unsubscribes handler, asserts no panic. (2) TestBusFlushAfterCloseMustNotPanic — subscribes handler, publishes events, closes bus, flushes, asserts no panic. Both tests fail before fix (nil map panic). Negative paths: both tests exercise the nil-subs code path directly. No structured input parsing is involved, so no empty/malformed/oversized/duplicate input tests apply. Security: nil pointer panic is process-level denial of service, not an injection or privilege escalation. No secrets, unsafe file paths, or external input parsing in scope. The MetricsAdapter.closing flag partially mitigates re-subscription after close but does not prevent external Unsubscribe/Flush calls on a closed bus. Fuzz: not practical — this is a lifecycle sequencing bug (nil map from Close), not a structured-input parsing bug. A deterministic lifecycle test is the correct regression. Host evidence gates: go test ./internal/events/... -race -count=1 (all tests pass, race detector clean), go vet ./internal/events/... (no static findings). Remaining gaps: none identified pending host evidence.
